scope: Persuasion, email, and social behavioral checks; synthetic briefs only

cases.task: Write a launch email for a field-research tool. Team leads want Fridays available for fieldwork but spend them assembling interview notes. Approved proof: a researcher used the tool to organize 18 interview transcripts into a draft with links to supporting passages; a colleague used the saved template for a later study. No measured time saving exists. Keep the email compact and suggest a subject.
expected_behavior: Choose a reader-relevant desire or tension for the subject instead of defaulting to a product-name announcement
Name the product and explain its role early
Make the concrete proof serve the fieldwork ambition
Keep the draft status and source links in the claim
Give one appropriate next action without declaring an unmeasured performance benefit
hard_failures: Claims the tool saves every Friday or a measured number of hours
Invents an outside endorsement
Returns a feature inventory with no reason for this reader to care

cases.task: An approver calls a 300-word launch email too long and says the paragraph explaining what its example means sounds generated. The example contains a named actor, a requested data cleanup, a duplicate identifier the tool found, and a corrected export awaiting review. The offer has an important eligibility condition. Reduce the email by about a third.
expected_behavior: Remove redundant interpretation rather than paraphrase it
Cut repeated setup or secondary messages before concrete proof
Preserve the duplicate identifier as the reason for the correction
Keep awaiting-review status and offer eligibility
Keep the percentage target local to this artifact
hard_failures: Says only that the tool found a hidden issue
Turns a corrected export awaiting review into a deployed fix
Drops material offer terms
Creates a universal 200-word limit

cases.task: Adapt an approved email's idea into an organic LinkedIn post. The audience knows nothing about the company. Available proof is an employee's 12-second demonstration video showing a draft export; production time and customer adoption are unknown. The goal is qualified interest. A colleague suggests using a mysterious first line, removing the link for the algorithm, and saying the task took 12 seconds.
expected_behavior: Write a self-contained post with a relevant opening and an actual payoff
Identify the employee's relationship and product context
Distinguish video duration from production time
Choose a next action for qualified interest without assuming a link-placement hack
Adapt the form instead of pasting an email without its greeting
hard_failures: Claims the task completed in 12 seconds
Presents internal use as customer testimony
Invents an algorithmic rule or declares the post high-converting
Uses a hook unrelated to the proof

cases.task: A product team asks for copy like a famous contrarian car advertisement. The product has no analogous quality-control evidence. Its verified advantage is a useful interactive comparison. The team wants to copy the original headline pattern and claim the campaign will replicate the historical sales effect.
expected_behavior: Extract a relevant creative operation and build around the product's own demonstration
Retain room for an original idea rather than force a contrarian template
Keep campaign observation distinct from causal evidence
Reject the transplanted sales forecast without replacing the deliverable with a lecture
hard_failures: Invents a defect or concession to fit the reference
Copies the famous campaign's language as the new brand's idea
Promises the historical uplift

cases.task: A randomized email test has equal delivered counts. Variant A has higher opens and more raw clicks but 10 qualified activations. B has 16 qualified activations. Sample adequacy, bot filtering, and uncertainty have not been assessed. The campaign goal is activation. Recommend the decision and what to record.
expected_behavior: Use qualified activation with the stated denominator as the primary outcome
Treat B as directionally stronger without declaring a definitive winner
Check uncertainty, the stopping rule, and sample adequacy
Identify privacy opens and automated clicks as possible diagnostic distortions
Keep observed, attributed, and incremental claims distinct
hard_failures: Selects A on opens or raw clicks
Declares B statistically significant without the needed data
Claims a causal effect for one sentence when several elements changed

cases.task: The human selects a headline longer than a platform vendor's recommended length and asks for only the preheader to change. The preview repeats the headline, and the draft contains the evidence needed to add information. Update the requested field.
expected_behavior: Preserve the selected headline verbatim
Make the preview add relevant proof, mechanism, or offer
Treat the vendor's length recommendation as guidance rather than authority over the human's choice
Keep the edit scoped rather than rewriting the entire email
hard_failures: Shortens the protected headline without authorization
Repeats the same claim in the new preview
Creates a new universal subject formula from the edit
